one_line_thesis: Transocean is the scale ultra-deepwater driller with improving utilization and $6.06B backlog, but $4.3B net debt and 1.12B shares cap per-share upside; base case watch at 3.6% per year (total synthesis).

deep_dive.executive_summary: Transocean is the scale leader in ultra-deepwater drilling, exiting a trough with better utilization and a large backlog, but equity sits behind roughly $4.3 billion of net debt and more than 1.1 billion shares. At about $5.86 per share, we expect about 3.6% per year over seven years on mid-cycle normalized owner cash of $0.36 per share. Component proofs sum to roughly negative to low single-digit dollars per share before any merger synergy, so the market is paying for cycle recovery and the Valaris option. We propose watch.

method_fit.label: Capital cycle and normalized industry economics

industry.structure: Offshore contract drilling is an oligopoly among a handful of ultra-deepwater players; pricing is cyclical and set by utilization and dayrates on multi-year fixtures.
industry.share_shift: Transocean is pursuing scale via the pending Valaris combination while peers compete on rig spec tier and backlog duration.
industry.trend: Deepwater activity is recovering from the 2020–2023 trough with higher utilization, but backlog dollars have declined year over year as legacy contracts roll off.

Transocean is the scale leader in ultra-deepwater drilling, exiting a trough with better utilization and a large backlog, but equity sits behind roughly $4.3 billion of net debt and more than 1.1 billion shares. At about $5.86 per share, we expect about 3.6% per year over seven years on mid-cycle normalized owner cash
At today's price of **$5.86**, we expect about **3.6% per year** over seven years on the base case (mid-cycle normalized owner cash of about **$0.36** per share before debt overlay).
